messages.subject: Multiple AR frailties by group
parts:
Hi,

I have a data set containing purchasing events by multiple subjects.  I'm modelling these purchases as repeated events by fitting a Weibull frailty model to the data.
I've implemented autoregressive dependence on the residuals (AR(1) frailty) resulting in one AR coefficient (rho) for all subjects. However,  I've assigned the individuals to different groups based on purchasing behavior.  
I was wondering if INLA is able to incorporate different autoregressive dependencies by subject group, thus assuming group-specific AR(1)'s?

Kind regards,

David

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multiple AR frailties by group
parts:
good question.

using time-dependent frailty will usually require a prior for the
correlation parameter that contracts to 1, see inla.doc("pc.cor1")

using 'replicate', like

f(time, model="ar1", replicate=subject)

with subject = 1, 2,...

then each person have its own realiation of the ar1 model, but they
all share the same hyperparameters (precision, correlation)

if you want to split this, then you need several terms,

f(time1, model="ar1", replicate=subject1) +
f(time2,
model="ar1", replicate=subject2)

where time1=time, time2=time, f.ex,

and subject1 = 1,2..., are those in 'group1'
and subject2 = 1, 2,... are those in 'group2'

then the (prec, corr) parameters will be separate for each group, but
the same within each group.

so, you cannot have to many groups then...

H
